relations.note: Edo tradition commonly describes Olókun as the creator's child or subordinate.
relations.source: Edo oral accounts collected by Izevbigie

relations.note: The creator assigns Olókun dominion over the sea and sometimes grants status, wealth, or a spouse.
relations.source: Edo oral accounts collected by Izevbigie

relations.myth: Contest for divine status and wealth
relations.note: Some Edo narratives have Olókun compete for status, wealth, or a spouse.
relations.source: Edo oral accounts collected by Izevbigie

relations.note: Female Ifẹ̀ Olókun is called Odùduwà's wife in regional oral history.
relations.source: Ifẹ̀ oral history in modern ethnography

relations.note: Some modern creation retellings make Olókun oppose Odùduwà's establishment of dry land.
Ọbàtálá restrains or chains Olokun after the sea threatens to inundate the world.
Some modern creation retellings make Olókun oppose Ọbàtálá's establishment of dry land.
Some Cuban versions have Òrúnmìlà divine against, mediate, or help bind the flooding Olokun.
relations.source: Recorded Ifá and Cuban ritual discourse

relations.note: Cuban Ifá establishes communication with Olokun through Orula's consecrated instruments.
Yemayá governs visible coastal waters while Olokun governs the deep ocean.
Some Cuban and transnational traditions make Olokun an older road or manifestation of Yemayá.
Some Cuban houses describe Olokun as Yemayá's parent.
Ajé is brought from or personified within Olokun's wealthy aquatic domain.
relations.source: Yoruba praise and modern ritual literature

relations.note: Some modern devotees identify the personified wealth-power as Ajé Olókun, though the equation is not universal.
A modern-recorded Edo narrative says Olókun meets or marries Imadese Mammy Wata.
Somú Gagá accompanies Olokun and represents life, masking, or the living aspect of the abyss.
Akaró accompanies Olokun, represents death, and is commonly paired with Somú Gagá.
Frobenius identified Olókun as an Atlantic African Poseidon within his discredited Atlantis hypothesis.
